conviction_note: Findings sum to +3.6 (a Q3 consensus of ~$66.3-66.6M that sits below Q2's $67.5M although last year's Q3 grew sequentially in both regions, a guide the company has raised three times that FY consensus sits under, and a 15%-of-float short with ~10 days to cover), but the scaled number is only (2*0.54-1)*10 = +0.8: a +17 vol-point put skew and 5.47 put/call OI argue the other way, the 5-day +10.5% run-up has already spent part of the squeeze, and this name sold a 3% beat-and-raise for -13.4% last quarter on international softness, so p_up sits barely above 50 while abs_move stays at the name's own ~9.5-10% median.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus ~$66.3M (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-10-21, https://finviz.com/news/405656/establishment-labs-faces-a-seasonal-test-of-its-us-boom-after-a-32-slide) and $66.6M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ESTA/earnings-forecasts; Tickflow ~$65M); EPS consensus about -$0.24 to -$0.32 (sources disagree). Company FY2026 revenue guide $269-271M (Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001688757/000168875726000047/estaerq22026-ex991.htm), implying H2 of about $141.7-143.7M on H1 of $127.3M. FY consensus about $268M per Earnings Whispers, below the low end of the guide. Revenue bar is sourced to two roughly agreeing estimate sources plus the company guide; the EPS bar is not reliable.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,017,107 shares = 14.98% of float, 9.8 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/ESTA/short-interest, FINRA publication 2026-10-26); 3.98M / 12.1 DTC on 9/30, 4.39M / 16.4% on 8/31 and 9/15, so shorts slightly covered after the Q2 sell-off but remain crowded. Baseline: 25-delta skew +16.97 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 5.47, no two-sided ATM quote so no option-implied move; 5-day run-up +10.53%, 20-day +7.27%, 28% below the 52-week high. Earnings Whispers described sentiment as having shifted from mildly bullish to clearly bearish after Q2. Insider record: only routine Form 4s (tax withholding by the CEO on 2026-08-20, director stock-in-lieu-of-retainer grants on 2026-09-30), no open-market buying or selling.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar (~$66.3-66.6M, Earnings Whispers and Benzinga) is BELOW Q2's $67.5M, yet in Q3 2025 both regions grew sequentially: US $10.3M to $11.9M (+16%) and OUS $41.0M to $41.9M. Holding OUS at 0-4% year over year (Q2 was +4.4%) gives $41.9-43.6M; reaching $66.3M then needs US of only $22.7-24.4M, i.e. a sequential DECLINE from Q2's $24.7M in a business that grew US +26% sequentially Q1 to Q2. Management said on the Q2 call it expects the US to 'remain strong' in Q3 with OUS following its normal seasonal pattern. A flat-to-up US quarter puts revenue near $68-70M, a 2.5-5% beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have been bought and sold: Q3 2025 beat on US Motiva sales, +22.49%; Q4 2025 +6.28%; Q1 2026 beat, +5.0%; Q2 2026 3.1% beat with a guide raise, -13.37%, because OUS growth slowed to 4.4% and Middle East orders fell. So the line the stock trades on is OUS and guidance quality, not the headline beat.
findings.source_date: 2025-11-05 (Q3 2025 release); Q2 2026 regional split from the 10-Q filed 2026-08 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001688757/000168875726000050/esta-20260630.htm); consensus from the Earnings Whispers preview dated 2026-10-21
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus models Q3 below Q2 on the 'seasonally softest quarter' framing. If the market were pricing a sequentially rising US quarter, the bar would sit above $67.5M and the put skew would not be +17 vol points with put OI 5.5x calls. The stock is still 28% off its high after the August drop.
findings.independence: Management's Q2 call commentary that the US should 'remain strong' in Q3 (call transcript, https://www.webull.com/news/15700165989565440) is a separate document from the arithmetic. It is the company's own forward statement, so it is not independent of the company. Shares the consensus source with the guidance finding.

findings.finding: FY consensus (~$268M per Earnings Whispers) sits below the low end of the company's $269-271M guide, which management has raised three quarters running, most recently on 2026-08-06 from $266.5-268.5M. Reaching the guide midpoint needs ~$143M in H2, against ~$142.5M in consensus (Q3 $66.6M + Q4 $76.2M on Benzinga). A Q3 at or above Q2 would make a fourth raise, or a first more specific 2027 frame (management has so far said only 'around 25%' growth), the likely guidance outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide raises have not reliably been rewarded: Q1 2026 raise (to $266.5-268.5M) +5.0%; Q2 2026 raise (to $269-271M) -13.37%. Q3 2025 'exceed $210M' raise +22.49%.
findings.why_not_priced: If a fourth raise were expected, FY consensus would sit at or above the guide midpoint rather than below its low end. The Middle East (<5% of revenue) is guided to stay depressed through year-end, so the guide already absorbs that headwind.
findings.independence: Same consensus sources as the reported-quarter finding (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-10-21; https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ESTA/earnings-forecasts). It rests partly on the same Q3 arithmetic, so the two are not fully independent.

findings.finding: Positioning: 4.02M shares short = 15.0% of float, 9.8 days to cover (2026-10-15 record), with 4.4M / 16.4% short at end-August. That is a crowded short into a print where the revenue bar sits below the last quarter. The 5-day run-up of +10.5% (from ~$61 on 2026-10-21 to $68.8) suggests some covering has begun.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +22.49% reaction in November 2025 came with short interest in a similar zone. No direct record of squeezes on this name beyond that.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is published but not in the baseline. The +17 put skew and 5.47 put/call OI show the market is paid to protect downside, so the squeeze asymmetry is not what options price. The 5-day run-up partly prices it, which is why this is sized below 1.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers 2026-10-21 describes sentiment as 'clearly bearish' (https://finviz.com/news/405656/establishment-labs-faces-a-seasonal-test-of-its-us-boom-after-a-32-slide). That is a separate source pointing to the same crowding.

findings.finding: Galderma reported on 2026-10-22, after ESTA last spoke: Q3 net sales +26.0% at constant currency, FY guide raised to 22.5-23.5% (from 19-21%). Fillers were soft but consumer aesthetics demand was broadly strong in Q3, which argues against a summer collapse in self-pay aesthetic procedures.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of ESTA reacting to Galderma prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy: injectables, not breast implants, and a different buyer decision. ESTA's stock has run +10% since; part of that may be this read-through.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Galderma does not sell breast implants.

findings.finding: Competitor POLYTECH (German implant maker, OUS-heavy) says its implant revenue grew 16.3% in Jan-Sep 2026 (B-LITE +83.5%), while ISAPS's 2025 survey shows global primary augmentation down ~2.2% and breast lifts up 48%. Read for ESTA's OUS business, the market is flat to slightly down and share is moving among premium/lighter implants. It is neutral net: a soft global volume base against evidence that premium OUS implant sellers are still growing double digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: OUS was the line that moved the stock -13.37% in August (OUS +4.4%).
findings.source_date: undated LinkedIn post; content cites Jan-Sep 2026, so it is October 2026 at the earliest (search snippet only, page returned HTTP 999)
findings.why_not_priced: A private competitor's promotional post is not aggregated anywhere, but it is weak and two-sided.

findings.finding: Financing: the Oaktree term loan was refinanced on 2026-04-30 ($265M Tranche E funded, $35M Tranche F on mutual consent, 8.75%, maturity 2031, no principal before maturity). The company elected 100% PIK interest through 2026-06-30. Covenants are minimum liquidity of $30M (cash was $71.2M) and minimum trailing-12-month sales (in compliance), with no going-concern language. Management guides FCF positive in H2 2026, so Q3 cash and whether PIK continues are on display. The money funded a ramp (US +141%, cash up $3.1M sequentially), so this is signed zero rather than as distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print has turned on the balance sheet since the refinancing.
findings.why_not_priced: The PIK election sits in the 10-Q footnote, not the release. A Q3 that shows cash burn into the seasonal low with PIK continuing would undercut the 'no further equity' message, while FCF-positive would confirm it. It is two-sided.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview notes management said no further equity raises are needed (finviz link above).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-05 FDA approved 28 additional Motiva SmoothSilk Round/Ergonomix sizes (down to 105cc), with US availability before year-end. That widens the US addressable range for Q4 and supports a firm Q4 guide; the stock rose +3.76% on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced on the day. What is left is whether management quantifies the Q4 contribution on the call.

outside_window.finding: The Motiva breast reconstruction PMA (submitted 2025-12-29) is in FDA review with BIMO site audits underway. Management expects no 2026 revenue and the 2027 ~25% growth plan assumes approval. A decision is not dated inside the window; only call commentary on timing could land on 2026-10-29.

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive, against a strong put skew (+17 vol points, P/C OI 5.47), and agree with the recent 5-day +10.5% run-up. The skew is consistent with a crowded short hedging and with a name that sold its last beat for -13%, so p_up was pulled to 54 rather than the ~57 the arithmetic alone would justify.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Q2's 3% beat-and-raise sold -13.4%, so the reported-quarter finding was cut from +2.0 to +1.5.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the PIK/refinancing funded a corroborated US ramp with covenant headroom ($71M cash vs $30M minimum), so it was re-signed from -0.3 to 0.0.
Lesson 7 (positioning / skew): a positive sign against a +17 skew moved p_up from 55 to 54. The crowded-short finding was trimmed from +1.0 to +0.8 because the 5-day run-up has partly spent it.
Two readings of one document: the guidance finding shares the consensus source and Q3 arithmetic with the reported-quarter finding, so it was trimmed from +1.0 to +0.8.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the revenue bar is sourced to two roughly agreeing estimates plus the company guide, so no cap was applied; the EPS bar is noted as unreliable and nothing is sized on it.
